deep.reconstruction:
The page is a torn fragment with two lines of Latin. The right edge is lost, so each line is cut off mid-word. Text (with my completion of the cut word in brackets):

"1) Determinentur inter superficies tribus lineis rectis te[rminatas] ... ubique evanescat seu quarum pars quaelibet finita [sit → corrected] ..."

Translation: "1) Let there be determined, among the surfaces bounded by three straight lines, [those for which some quantity] vanishes everywhere, or of which every finite part [is of minimal area / has ...]."

There is no derivation, only the statement of a problem. The phrasing "[some quantity] ubique evanescat" followed by the equivalent "seu quarum pars quaelibet finita ..." is the standard way of stating the minimal-surface (Plateau) problem. The vanishing quantity is presumably the mean curvature, i.e. the sum of the principal curvatures, or equivalently the first variation of area. My reading of the modern statement: find surfaces S with boundary consisting of three straight lines such that H = 0 on S, equivalently every finite piece of S has least area among surfaces with the same boundary. In nonparametric form this is the minimal surface equation: (1+z_y^2) z_xx - 2 z_x z_y z_xy + (1+z_x^2) z_yy = 0.

This matches the problem Riemann treated in 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', published posthumously in 1867 by Hattendorff. That paper handles minimal surfaces bounded by systems of straight lines through the Gauss map and the hypergeometric / conformal-mapping method, and includes examples with several (infinite) straight lines. I recall rather than verified that it treats the three-line case specifically. The '1)' suggests this is the first item of a list of problems or examples.

No computation is present on this page, and nothing can be reconstructed beyond the problem statement. The next page is illegible.

results.what: Statement of the problem: determine surfaces bounded by three straight lines whose mean curvature vanishes everywhere, i.e. every finite part has minimal area.
results.modern_name: Plateau problem for minimal surfaces with polygonal (straight-line) boundary; minimal surface equation H=0
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1760, minimal surface equation), Meusnier (1776, H=0), Plateau (1849/1873, experiments). Riemann (lectures c. 1860-61, publ. 1867) and Weierstrass (1866) for polygonal boundaries; later Schwarz.
